turn_text: Well, so for over 15 years, it's been the law in this country that insurance companies need to cover people's mental health care needs, just like they do physical health care. That's the law. And we have Minnesota Senator Paul Wellstone to thank for that. He passed this law and championed it, you know, as I said, over 15 years ago. But I think we also know that for years, insurance companies have been finding ways to get around this law. And I've been working to fix these loopholes since I came to the Senate. So this is why it's so important that the President Biden and Vice President Harris put out this new rule in the last week to tighten up and close these loopholes. And I'm just really grateful for that. I think we all know what insurance companies can do with mental health care treatment. They will do prior authorizations that make it almost impossible to get care. They will require you to go through different steps of care, even though your doctor has said that you need step C, they say no, you have to do step A and B first. They just throw up a lot of barriers. And so this new rule will increase the price that insurance companies pay for going through that and will require them to drop some of that red tape. So it's a big deal and I'm excited that they've made this headway.

There absolutely is more that we need to do. A couple of things that I am working on is one is to try to increase the number of people that are going into the field of mental health care. Another thing that's important is to continue to support access to tele-mental health, which is something that we started doing during the pandemic. And it has been a real godsend for people who find that in some cases it's better for them to be able to do a video call with a therapist or a counselor rather than having to leave the house and drive long distances which might just not be practical for them. So those are two additional things that I think would help expand access to mental health care.
